xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3922: Deacon-lite: relay run status from the deacon child to the dashboard; watchdog stale verdict

plan.title: Deacon-lite: relay run status from the deacon child to the dashboard; watchdog stale verdict
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5-1

narratives.Problem: GET /api/deacon/status and GET /api/cloister/status read getDeaconLiteStatus() from the dashboard process, but deacon-lite runs only inside the forked deacon child (deacon-main.ts), so every consumer (pan admin cloister status, the DeaconStatus widget, DeaconActivityView, the core-services row, and the pan up supervisor watchdog) sees running:false and lastRunAt:null. The watchdog's stale verdict was neutralised in c8a7c0f for this reason, so a wedged deacon is invisible. A manual patrol (POST /api/deacon/patrol) also bypasses the child's tick(), so it never stamps status even locally.
narratives.Proposal: Keep status in memory and file-free (PAN-3917 W4). Add one child-to-parent IPC message: deacon-lite gains a setPatrolRunObserver seam and an exported runDeaconLitePatrol tick; deacon-main registers an observer that sends {type:'patrol-done', at, error} after every tick and routes the manual patrol through the tick; the deacon supervisor stores the latest report (kept across child restarts) and exports lastPatrolReport; the control surface composes deaconLite from the supervisor (running = child running, intervalMs = the exported constant, lastRunAt/lastRunError = the report); the supervisor watchdog reads deaconLite.intervalMs and deaconLite.lastRunAt only, keeping the c8a7c0f missing-means-no-verdict rule. No new routes, no disk writes, no frontend changes.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Restoring the pre-cut 'heartbeat missing for N seconds' watchdog verdict; a null lastRunAt still yields no verdict.
- Persisting run status to disk or the event store; no patrol log ring; GET /api/deacon/logs stays empty.
- Changing src/cli/commands/cloister/status.ts; its dead DeaconStatusResponse.lastPatrol block (lines 15-22, 87-92) is left as-is.
- Any frontend source change; DeaconStatus.tsx and DeaconActivityView.tsx already render the relayed fields.
- A re-entrancy guard on runDeaconLitePatrol for overlapping slow ticks.
- Resetting the stored patrol report when the deacon child respawns.
- Relaying through the deacon event client / event store instead of IPC.

autoDecisions.summary: Relay over the existing fork() IPC channel, not the deacon event client.
autoDecisions.rationale: IPC already carries patrol and reload-config; a run-status ping needs no durability, batching, or sequence numbers, and the issue body names this transport.

autoDecisions.summary: The supervisor keeps the last patrol report across child respawns.
autoDecisions.rationale: Resetting on respawn would blind the watchdog to a child that restarts but never completes a patrol, which is exactly the case the neutralised verdict cannot see; keeping it is also less code.

autoDecisions.summary: deaconLite.running in the dashboard's composed status means the deacon child process is running (isChildRunning()).
autoDecisions.rationale: The child starts deacon-lite as part of Cloister start and exits with code 1 when that fails, so process liveness is the honest proxy; the CLI already renders running-with-null-lastRunAt as 'waiting for first run'.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep the c8a7c0f behaviour: a null lastRunAt produces no watchdog verdict; only a stale or unparsable reported timestamp restarts.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for the stale verdict to read the relayed value; restoring the missing-timestamp verdict re-opens the restart loop risk on slow first patrols and was deliberately removed.

autoDecisions.summary: The watchdog reads deaconLite.intervalMs and deaconLite.lastRunAt only; the config.patrolIntervalMs and state.lastPatrol reads and their test fixtures are removed/migrated.
autoDecisions.rationale: Those fields belonged to the deleted deacon and can never appear in /api/deacon/status again; leaving the fallback chain makes the staleness threshold ignore the real interval and turns seven test fixtures into no-ops.

autoDecisions.summary: Manual patrols (POST /api/deacon/patrol) run through the exported tick so they stamp and relay status.
autoDecisions.rationale: Today deacon-main calls runDeaconLite() directly, so the DeaconActivityView 'Run patrol now' button can never move lastRunAt; routing through the tick fixes that with a one-line change.

autoDecisions.summary: No frontend changes; documentation goes to docs/DASHBOARD-ARCHITECTURE.md (new deacon-child block) and sync-sources/skills/pan-admin-cloister/SKILL.md (status bullet).
autoDecisions.rationale: Both widgets already read deaconLite.lastRunAt/lastRunError/running; the architecture doc has no deacon-child section at all and the skill is the operator-facing description of status.

metadata.sizeJustification: Six subsystems by the first-two-segment rule (src/lib, src/dashboard, src/supervisor, tests/unit, docs, sync-sources/skills) at the limit, not over it; the change is one relay path end to end and cannot be split without shipping a dashboard that still reports running:false.

items.title: deacon-lite: export the interval, an exported patrol tick, and a patrol-run observer seam

expected_outputs: tests/unit/lib/cloister/deacon-lite.test.ts passes including the new runDeaconLitePatrol describe block

narrative.Action: PRD W1. In src/lib/cloister/deacon-lite.ts: (1) export DEACON_LITE_INTERVAL_MS (line 179); (2) add `export interface PatrolRunReport { at: string; error: string | null }`, a module-level `patrolRunObserver`, and `export function setPatrolRunObserver(fn | null)` in the style of setAgentStoppedNotifier (line 107); (3) rename `async function tick()` (line 185) to `export async function runDeaconLitePatrol()`, keep its try/catch stamping of lastRunAt/lastRunError, and after the try/catch call the observer with { at: lastRunAt, error: lastRunError } inside its own try/catch that only console.errors; update the two tick() call sites in startDeaconLite (lines 199-200); (4) update the module docstring (lines 9-11) to say the child relays each completed tick through setPatrolRunObserver (PAN-3922). Tests: extend the import destructure at tests/unit/lib/cloister/deacon-lite.test.ts:77 and add the five cases listed in the PRD (clean run reports {at, error:null} and stamps lastRunAt; a rejected reconcileClosedIssueAgents reports error text; a globally paused tick still reports; a throwing observer is swallowed; DEACON_LITE_INTERVAL_MS is 60_000). Reset the observer to null in afterEach. In each new case set mocks.listAgentStates.mockReturnValue([]) and mocks.liveAgentInventory.mockResolvedValue(inventory([])) as the existing runDeaconLite block does, otherwise checkStuckWorkAgents iterates undefined and the clean-run case reports an error. Use the existing fake timers/system time.

narrative.Action: PRD W6. (1) docs/DASHBOARD-ARCHITECTURE.md: after the 'Server structure' bullet list and before '**Two WebSocket endpoints:**', add a '**Deacon child process:**' block in the file's bold-lead bullet style stating: the dashboard forks dist/dashboard/deacon.js (src/dashboard/server/deacon-main.ts) through services/deacon-supervisor.ts; Cloister and deacon-lite run only in that child; IPC carries parent→child {type:'patrol'} and {type:'reload-config'} and child→parent {type:'patrol-done', at, error} after every completed tick (PAN-3922); the supervisor keeps the latest report across child restarts; GET /api/deacon/status and GET /api/cloister/status compose deaconLite from it (running = child process running, intervalMs = 60000, lastRunAt/lastRunError = the report); the pan up supervisor watchdog restarts the dashboard when deaconLite.lastRunAt is older than three intervals and never on a null timestamp. (2) sync-sources/skills/pan-admin-cloister/SKILL.md: extend the `status` bullet (line 38) to say the 'Deacon loop:' line shows the last patrol the deacon child relayed (lastRunAt, lastRunError), that 'waiting for first run' means the child is up but has not completed a tick, and that a last run older than three minutes prints red and is the same condition on which the supervisor watchdog restarts the dashboard.
